## Who reviews Each pull request gets two reviews: the independent review before each push (`before-push.md`), and the PR review, which gives the merge verdict. The scripts are in `~/.agents/skills/way-of-working/scripts/`. Whether the Cursor bot is available decides which tool does which: | Cursor bot | Independent review: the first available, in this order | PR review | |---|---|---| | Available | 1. Kimi on K3.1 Pro at high effort: `herdr-review.sh --kind kimi`
2. Pi: `pi-review.sh --role independent`
3. Codex on gpt-6-luna: `herdr-review.sh` | The Cursor bot | | Not available | 1. Kimi on K3.1 Pro at high effort: `herdr-review.sh --kind kimi`
2. Codex on gpt-6-luna: `herdr-review.sh`
3. The Cursor agent CLI: `herdr-review.sh --kind cursor` | Pi: `pi-review.sh --role pr` | Each order leaves out the tool that gives the PR review, so rule 5 below holds whichever reviewer runs. A reviewer is not available when it cannot start here, when its run fails with an error (Pi through Ollama returns 429 at its weekly usage limit), or when it gives no report within its hour and has stopped. `pi-review.sh` stops Pi at the hour itself. When `herdr-review.sh` ends without a report, run its `Next:` command first, because the review may still be running; the reviewer counts as not available only when that command also ends without a report and `herdr agent get ` shows the reviewer idle or done, not working (in Rex, first read `rex block call -s -b program_status` and keep waiting while it says working or blocked; then confirm with `rex block call -s -b process` whether the reviewer's program still runs; only then do two looks a minute apart with `rex capture -s -b ` that show the same screen, with the reviewer's empty input line and no busy marker, count as idle; in the Herdr app, `hc get ` shows the terminal finished, or its status idle or done, and for a reviewer that reports no status, two looks a minute apart with `hc read ` show the same screen with its empty input line). While it is still working, keep waiting for it. Then try the next one in the order. When every reviewer in the order is not available, push nothing: tell the owner, and wait for a reviewer that differs from the PR reviewer. `herdr-review.sh` runs in a Herdr TUI pane, inside Rex, where it hands off to `rex-review.sh`, or in the Herdr app, where it hands off to `hc-review.sh`. Outside all three, Kimi and the Cursor agent CLI are not available, and Codex runs through the Codex plugin, as `before-push.md` says. Say in the PR body which reviewer ran, and why each one before it in the order did not. 1. **Before the pull request opens, pick the row from what the bot did on the repository's most recent pull request**, the newest one by creation, whether it is open, merged or closed. If the bot posted a review of the head commit, or merged the pull request itself, within 20 minutes of that pull request's last push, the mark in rule 2, use the "Available" row, even when that review counted only as a comment there. If it did not, use the "Not available" row. A merged pull request still shows every time this needs: - the head commit: `gh pr view --json headRefOid,mergedAt,mergedBy`, which also shows a merge by the bot; - the last push: `gh api repos///commits//check-suites`, each suite's `created_at`. A commit's own date is when it was written, which can be long before its push; - the check's start: `gh pr checks --json name,startedAt`; - each review's commit and time: `gh api repos///pulls//reviews`. A review of an earlier commit does not count. Judge the bot's behaviour, not the row that pull request used: a pull request on the "Not available" row reads the bot's answers as comments, so copying its row would keep every later pull request on that row after the bot came back. For a repository's first pull request, use the "Available" row. On the "Not available" row, Pi is the PR reviewer from the first push: start it on every push without waiting for the bot, and read any answer from the bot as a comment. 2. **After each push, give the bot 20 minutes.** A bot that has not answered at 9 minutes may still be reviewing (the owner, 2026-10-30: "the fact that Cursor did not get back in 9 mins does nt mean cursor bot stops reviewing it"). `merge-on-verdict.sh --timeout 1200 --bot-check "Cursor Automation"` waits for its verdict (the bot's check is named "Cursor Automation" on this owner's repositories). The bot is not available when it has posted no verdict 20 minutes after the push (exit 5), or sooner when its check has finished without one, skipped or "encountered an error" (exit 7), since then it is no longer reviewing. 3. **When the bot is not available, start Pi as the PR reviewer yourself, on top of what the bot already did:** `pi-review.sh --role pr --pr --head `, with `--since ` after the first round. Read everything the bot and its companions (Bugbot) posted on the pull request first, fix or answer each finding, and give the reviewer that list with what became of each item, so it checks those and goes on from there instead of starting over. Nothing starts it for you. Its MERGE or HOLD comment is the answer you wait for on that push. If the script exits 1, run it once more; if it fails again, log it and leave the pull request open. 4. **A switch lasts for the rest of the pull request. Stop the bot's run on that head before its stand-in starts**, so two reviewers do not work on one push or race their verdicts. When `merge-on-verdict.sh --bot-check` exits 7, or exits 5 saying "with no verdict from" the bot (an exit 5 that says it was waiting for the check "with the bot's MERGE in hand" is not a missing verdict: wait for the check, and switch nothing), and before `pi-review.sh --role pr` (or the stand-in the project names) starts: 1. Run `~/.agents/skills/way-of-working/scripts/stop-cursor-review.sh ` from the repository, or with `--repo `. It finds the bot's agent through the bot's check run on that head, cancels the agent's latest run through Cursor's Cloud Agents API, and adds the label `review-takeover` to the pull request, creating the label if the repository lacks it. It reads the API key from `CURSOR_API_KEY` or from `~/.config/cursor/api.env`; never commit the key. It leaves Bugbot and other Cursor agents alone. Exit 3 means something could not be checked or done, such as no key, no bot check run or a cancel the API refused, and says what: start the stand-in anyway, since the owner's recipe makes the switch even when the stop fails, and the bot may then still answer; read that answer as a comment. Exit 4 means the pull request is no longer at that head: start no stand-in for it, and wait for the bot on the new head. 2. Where the bot is a Cursor Automation, its owner adds a rule once per repository in the Cursor dashboard: skip pull requests labelled `review-takeover`. Without that rule, the next push starts the bot again. Tell the owner if the rule is missing. 3. Do not convert the pull request to a draft as the stop. A draft does not cancel a run already in progress. From then on the stand-in gives the verdict on every push, and the independent review follows the "Not available" row's order. A later answer from the bot is read as a comment, not as the verdict. 5. **The two reviews of the merged commit come from different tools.** Its independent review and its merge verdict must not both come from Pi, or both from Cursor. When the row changes after an independent review ran, and the tool that ran it now gives the PR review, run the first available reviewer in the new row's order on the head commit at once, and fix or answer its findings. Check again before you merge. The project or the owner can name other reviewers; the same rules then apply to the ones they name. When a reviewer in the order is not available, tell the owner which one and why, in the PR body or the session's report. `pi-review.sh` runs Pi in a fresh clone under `/tmp`, never in the working tree, because a reviewer that checks out a commit changes the files under your feet. As the independent reviewer it can review a commit that is not pushed yet, named by a short or full hash; it writes a report whose first line is READY or FIX, and posts nothing. A `--since` that names no commit, or that does not reach the clone, stops the run before Pi starts. As the PR reviewer it posts one comment whose first line is MERGE or HOLD, whose second line is `Reviewed commit: `, and whose last line is a mark unique to the run; the script fails unless a comment with that mark, that first line and that commit appears on the PR. A comment that names a commit other than the head is a verdict on that older commit. `--verify ""` names what to check, as for `herdr-review.sh`. Inside Herdr, Pi runs in its own tab, `pi--`, so the owner can watch; the tab closes only when every check passed. As the PR reviewer it refuses a `--head` that is not the pull request's head, and fails if the head moved while Pi reviewed. Pi gets an hour, then the script stops it and exits 1. It stops the whole process group, because `ollama launch` runs Pi as a child and does not pass the signal on; inside Herdr, that is the tab's foreground group. A passed run removes its clone. As the independent reviewer it keeps its report and prints the path as `Report:` on standard error, so output cut short can be read again. A failed run keeps the clone and its log to read. It needs Ollama and Pi installed (`ollama launch pi`). `scripts/test_pi_review.py` covers each case. ## What the body says - **While the Cursor bot is the PR reviewer, wait up to 20 minutes after each push for its verdict**, as "Who reviews" says, with `merge-on-verdict.sh --timeout 1200 --bot-check "Cursor Automation"` (exit 5: 20 minutes passed with no verdict; exit 7: the bot's check finished with none; after a MERGE the deadline becomes the later of start + `--timeout` and start + one hour, and an exit 5 then says it was waiting for the check, not for the bot), because `watch-pr.sh` does not wake on a check that only starts. If it is not available (exit 7, or exit 5 with no verdict from the bot; an exit 5 with its MERGE in hand is only a slow check), stop its run with `stop-cursor-review.sh` ("Who reviews", rule 4). On its exit 0 or 3 start Pi as the PR reviewer yourself; on its exit 4 the pull request has a new head, so start nothing and wait for the bot on that head. The 20 minutes is the wait for a verdict; the stop is what keeps the bot from reviewing on after its stand-in starts, and when the stop fails (exit 3) any later answer from the bot is a comment. - **Run `~/.agents/skills/way-of-working/scripts/watch-pr.sh `** from the repository as a background job the harness reports back on. It polls every 30 seconds and exits on the first new event: a merge or close, a new review, conversation comment or inline review comment, or a check that finishes, including a rerun that finishes with the same result. A check that only starts or reruns wakes nothing. It exits at once if the pull request has already merged. When it exits, read what changed, act, and start it again unless the pull request is merged or closed. Report only changes; silence is the normal case. - **Where the project lets you merge on the PR reviewer's verdict, run `~/.agents/skills/way-of-working/scripts/merge-on-verdict.sh `** as a background job, from the pull request's repository or with `--repo `. It waits for the bot's MERGE or HOLD review on that head (older commits never count; leading HTML comments are stripped), then for the required check (`--check`, default `checks`), and merges with `--match-head-commit` only on MERGE plus a passed check. It never bypasses branch rules, with one exception the owner must authorize: `--admin-if-only-review` lets it merge with admin privileges when GitHub refuses the merge because a required approving review is missing (for example, an approval agent that asks for a human on medium-risk changes) and nothing else is open: every check on the head passed, the head is not behind its base where the base's rules require an up-to-date branch (the script reads the rules and compares, since GitHub reports BLOCKED, not BEHIND, while a review is also missing), and no current review thread is unresolved. Ask the owner once whether they want that; if they do, record their words in a decision record, pass the flag on every merge, and the script says so in a comment on each pull request it merges this way. It never merges past a HOLD, a failed or pending check, a required update from the base, an open thread or a new head. When an admin merge must wait, it says why once (for example, an unresolved review thread or a check that has not passed), so a wait that will never end shows. Where the project requires a section in every PR body, pass `--require-section `: the script merges only when the body, as GitHub renders it, has a heading with exactly that text, ignoring the case of ASCII letters only ("État" does not match "état"). GitHub's renderer decides what is a heading, so a line in a code block or a comment never counts. Its exit code says what stopped it: 0 merged at the given head, by it or by someone else; 1 closed without a merge, or gh failed ten times in a row; 2 a HOLD; 3 a failed check; 4 a new head, or a pull request merged at another head (the wrong repository's pull request of that number); 5 timed out (with `--bot-check`: no verdict within `--timeout`, or, after a MERGE, the required check not finished by the later of start + `--timeout` and start + one hour; the message says which); 6 the body lacks the required section; 7 with `--bot-check`, the bot's check finished with no verdict, so start its stand-in; 64 a usage error. A loop written for the occasion is how a merge on a failed check gets through. - **Bound review output.** Use `gh api --jq` to select the reviewed commit, creation time, state, and relevant body text. Omit decorative HTML footers. Keep unresolved findings from earlier commits available until fixed or answered. Retrieve source text needed to judge a finding even when it is from an older round. - **After each push, leave the pull request alone until its reviewer answers**, with a hold or a merge. Make no other push, force-push, rebase or edit to its description in the meantime: a change that lands while the reviewer reads makes its verdict name a commit that is no longer the head, and the round is wasted. Work on something else while you wait. If the reviewer is not available (see "Who reviews"), Pi's verdict on the same commit is the answer you wait for. A problem you find while waiting is fixed after the answer: with the hold's findings, or, after a MERGE, as a new push that starts a new round before you merge. - **When the bot's verdict on the latest push names a pending CI check as its only blocker, and that check then passes, push an empty commit to ask it again.** The bot runs on pushes, not on finished checks, so its answer stays "not yet" until something is pushed. Do not merge by hand in its place: the merged commit then carries no verdict from its PR reviewer. - **Before each push to an open pull request, confirm it is still open** (`gh pr view --json state` returns `OPEN`). A `MERGED` or `CLOSED` pull request takes no more pushes. A bot can merge it while you work on the next fix, and a push to the merged branch reaches no reviewer: those commits then have to move to a new branch and pull request. - **On a HOLD**, fix on the same branch, run the check script again, run the independent review again, within its round limit (`before-push.md`), and reply on the PR saying what changed. - **A review against an older commit is not the current verdict.** Read the commit the review names before acting on it. - **On merge, run `~/.agents/skills/way-of-working/scripts/after-merge.sh `.** It syncs `main`, then deletes the branch locally and on the remote only if every commit on it is in `main`. Just before the remote delete, it moves every open pull request based on the branch to `main` with `gh`, because GitHub closed such a pull request when its base branch was deleted with `git push --delete` (enterprise-performance-model #328); if `gh` cannot list or move them, it deletes nothing, and if the run then fails, it moves them back while the remote lists the branch, leaves them on `main` if the branch is gone or the remote cannot be read (naming them to check by hand), and names any it cannot move back. A squash or rebase merge, or a commit pushed after the merge, leaves work outside `main`, and the script then deletes nothing. It reads the live remote and deletes under a lease on the commit it checked, so a push landing after the check makes the delete fail rather than lose that work. If the branch vanishes mid-run, because a review bot deleted it on merge, a failed fetch or delete counts as done only when git's error says the ref is missing and the live remote then lists no such branch. The script trusts the remote to list every branch; on a server that hides refs, a hidden branch looks deleted. It reads and deletes through the remote's one push URL, and stops if there are several, deleting nothing. Locally it uses `git branch -d`, which refuses an unmerged branch. `scripts/test_pr_scripts.py` covers a squash merge, a late push, an unpushed local commit, a remote branch already deleted, one deleted before the fetch or before the delete, a failed remote lookup, a fetch that wrongly reports the ref missing, a refused delete of a hidden ref, several push URLs, a push racing the delete, a commit racing `branch -d`, a stacked pull request moved before the delete, a failed listing that deletes nothing, a delete refused by the server or by the lease after the move, which moves the pull requests back, a move back that fails, which is named, a branch deleted by someone else during the moves, which leaves the moved pull requests on `main`, and a remote that cannot be read after a failed move, which leaves them on `main` and names them. - **Delete only a branch you opened.** A branch someone else opened is theirs to delete, even after its pull request merges. Ask. ## Rules that save review rounds

strip='gsub("^(\\s*<!--[\\s\\S]*?-->)+\\s*"; "")'

# Sets REPLY to "<MERGE|HOLD> <review-id>" for the bot's newest verdict on the full head $1,
# or to nothing. --paginate runs the filter once per page, so the filter prints one line per
# verdict and the last line, from the last page, is the newest.
verdict() {
  call gh api --paginate "repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/$number/reviews" --jq "
    .[] | select(.user.login == \"$bot\" and .commit_id == \"$1\")
        | ((.body | $strip | capture(\"^(\\\\*\\\\*)?(?<v>MERGE\\\\b|HOLD\\\\b|Held\\\\.)\")) // {} | .v) as \$v
        | select(\$v != null) | (if \$v == \"Held.\" then \"HOLD\" else \$v end) as \$v
        | \"\(\$v) \(.id)\"" || return 1
  REPLY=$(printf '%s\n' "$REPLY" | sed '/^$/d' | tail -n 1)
}

# Delivery playbook: engineering data to a validated graph

Status: Draft, version 0.1. Started 2026-10-13.

This playbook is for a team building a pipeline that turns engineering source data,
such as a P&ID authoring database or an exchange file, into a validated, queryable
graph. It records what to do, what worked, and what did not. It describes
engineering practice only. How the work itself flows (pull requests, reviews,
decision records and checks) is in the
[way-of-working standard](https://github.com/aadehamid/personal-agent-skills/tree/main/skills/engineering/way-of-working).

## How to read an entry

Each practice carries one status, and says what the status rests on.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Proven | A merged test or a recorded run shows that the practice works. |
| Proposed | The team decided on it, but has not built or tested it yet. |
| Didn't work | The team tried it and dropped it. The entry says why. |

Worked examples come from the project that started this playbook, a synthetic
P&ID pipeline that generates DEXPI files from a vendor-style backend and publishes
a graph. They are there to make a practice concrete. Adapt them; do not copy them.

## 1. Choose and pin the exchange standard

Status: Proposed. It rests on a review of the standard's releases and of the
tools available for it.

===

Status: Proposed. It rests on repeated failures to fetch the standard's
model files from their published host.

1. **Do not fetch at validation time.** If a schema or model file imports others
   from a remote host, a check that fetches them depends on that host's uptime and
   certificate.
2. **Keep a pinned copy in the repository.** Take it from the standard's release
   tag or official supporting materials. Store its SHA-256, its source and its
   attribution next to it.
3. **Map each import to its local copy.** Have the validator resolve imports
   through a table of pinned files, and turn off network access in the XML parser.
4. **Never disable certificate checks.** If a host fails TLS verification, record
   the failure and use the pinned copy.
5. **Do not generate a missing official file.** If no official source has the
   file, stop and escalate. A file you wrote yourself is not the standard.

# LIONG-REF-001 Reference register

| Document control | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | Draft for review |
| Version | 0.1 |
| Inspection date | 2026-10-05 UTC |
| Dependencies | [LIONG-001 charter](LIONG-001-charter.md), [LIONG-002 users and requirements](LIONG-002-users-and-requirements.md) |
| Authority | Consolidated evidence register for sources, ontology mappings, and technology assessment |
| Vocabulary authority | [GLOSSARY.md](../GLOSSARY.md) |

## Scope and evidence rules

All entries were accessed on 2026-10-05 UTC unless stated otherwise. Public HTTP requests inspected publisher pages, raw artifacts, and repository metadata. No paid-credit API, private-code submission, deployment, or implementation was used.

An inspected source supports only the claims listed in its entry. A live URL is not an immutable release pin. A license observation is not clearance of every file or imported dependency. All proposed reuse remains pending review under LIONG-003. Record adoption decisions in [LIONG-REG-001](LIONG-REG-001-decisions.md).

Local baseline documents read were [REQUIREMENTS.md](../REQUIREMENTS.md), [GLOSSARY.md](../GLOSSARY.md), [PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md](../PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md), and [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md). These govern LIONG scope; external sources do not amend them.

The package index resolves related documents. Their inclusion does not approve their proposals.

## REF-PPC-001: PPC documentation reference

- Source: [pinned repository](https://github.com/aadehamid/pearland-petroleum-corporation/tree/01027a84be5d453cbb4e2ea091e4884729918b15).
- Version inspected: commit `01027a84be5d453cbb4e2ea091e4884729918b15`.
- Paths inspected: recursive repository tree and [`docs/PPC-019_Public_Ontology_Reuse_and_Implementation_Guide.md`](https://github.com/aadehamid/pearland-petroleum-corporation/blob/01027a84be5d453cbb4e2ea091e4884729918b15/docs/PPC-019_Public_Ontology_Reuse_and_Implementation_Guide.md).
- Supported claims: PPC-019 version 0.1 calls its recommendations proposed and states that no ontology adoption is asserted. Implementation areas, including `semantic/ontology`, `semantic/mappings`, `schemas`, and `tests`, contain `.gitkeep` placeholders.
- Reuse/license status: reference for documentation patterns only. No license file found in the inspected tree. No copied prose, ontology files, or code authorized by this assessment.
- Unresolved gates: permission before copying any material; independent LIONG approval before adopting a pattern. PPC's EPM/ECE dependency and authority structure do not apply automatically.

## Standards, vocabularies, and compatibility references

### REF-STD-001: DEXPI specification and native XML

- Source: [official specifications](https://dexpi.org/specifications/), [2.0 HTML](https://dexpi.org/specification/2.0/html/), and [DEXPI XML definitions](https://dexpi.org/specification/2.0/html/basics/metamodel_and_exchange_format.html).
- Version inspected: 2.0 HTML identifies release 2.0.0 dated 2025-10-10. Landing page inspected live on the access date.
- Artifact inspected: [`_static/DEXPI_XML_Schema.xsd`](https://dexpi.org/specification/2.0/html/_static/DEXPI_XML_Schema.xsd). SHA-256 `0bd6568b7c52fd59ac4ef6d8547ab2b2aa890c009a3a1bfbc5d7cc18c53b36e6`. Its schema `version` is `1.0.0`; the linking page calls the download `DEXPI_XML_Schema_RC_1.xsd`.
- Supported claims: 2.0 uses DEXPI XML for models and instances, without requiring Proteus XML schema. The root is `Model`. File-local IDs and imported name references have distinct syntax. Model classes and properties require more than generic XML parsing.
- Additional observation: the landing page recommends 2.0.1 as a fix release replacing 2.0 and links [2.0.1 HTML](https://dexpi.org/specification/2.0.1/html/). The linked 2.0.1 artifacts were not inspected on that date; the 2026-10-14 point below records them.
- 2.0.1 observations, accessed 2026-10-13: the [release announcement](https://dexpi.org/dexpi-2-0-1-specification-published-the-update-replacing-dexpi-2-0/) dates 2.0.1 to 2026-09-30 and calls it the update replacing 2.0. It says 2.0.1 fixes a small number of issues in the Plant model and improves the Process model. The [specification repository](https://gitlab.com/dexpi/Specification) has a V2.0.1 tag holding the XSD and a 2.0.1 reference P&ID. The specification defines DEXPI XML as its exchange encoding; no other encoding was found. No official 2.0 validator was found. LIONG targets 2.0.1 ([DEC-061](decisions/DEC-061-dexpi-2-0-1.md)); its pinned artifacts are listed in the next point.
- 2.0.1 pins, retrieved 2026-10-14 ([DEC-074](decisions/DEC-074-dexpi-2-0-1-pinned-files.md)): the V2.0.1 tag is commit `eef0f0c6e8edfe84582e7a45d109c396bdc544f8`. From the tag, `DEXPI_XML_Schema.xsd` (SHA-256 `0bd6568b7c52fd59ac4ef6d8547ab2b2aa890c009a3a1bfbc5d7cc18c53b36e6`, the same bytes as the 2.0.0 download) and `reference_pid.xml` (`acd39c74292aef3f6f00581fc78b05814acf2318815abd28c14ebefba12fdd94`). The tag holds the models only as source for `dexpi.specificator`. From the [published 2.0.1 specification](https://dexpi.org/specification/2.0.1/html/)'s `_static` folder, `Core.xml` (`7136f8440c08c8bf7759c4e9eb614b046cc3196f2f45695122629a2020e61e4a`) and `Plant.xml` (`0a5175535c1263464fee653c7b99f38eb810c15824f84155748eac165f50edbf`). Building the tag's source with `dexpi.specificator` 1.0.1 (PyPI, MIT, wheel SHA-256 `410be144920a8039a6da4b71263755e184466a27fd9a2a00d8c1a1d7835de67c`) gave byte-identical `Core.xml`, `Plant.xml` and `Process.xml`. All three models import `MetaData.xml`, which DEXPI does not publish; the tool defines it in code. The 2.0.1 site states CC BY 4.0 for the specification. The copies are in `standards/dexpi/2.0.1` with their manifest.
- Reuse/license status: 2.0 specification explicitly states [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Confirm scope for separately packaged downloads and preserve attribution and modification notices.
- Unresolved gates: reconcile schema label versus artifact name; test syntax, schema, semantic rules, and engineering fidelity separately. No conformance test was run. Settled: the exact release is 2.0.1 ([DEC-061](decisions/DEC-061-dexpi-2-0-1.md)), and its imported models are pinned with their hashes, except `MetaData.xml`, which DEXPI does not publish ([DEC-074](decisions/DEC-074-dexpi-2-0-1-pinned-files.md)).

### REF-STD-002: QUDT

- Source: [official schema](https://qudt.org/schema/qudt/), fetched as RDF text.
- Version inspected: live schema labels itself `QUDT Schema - Version 3.5.2`. Its `owl:versionIRI` is the unversioned `http://qudt.org/schema/qudt`, so the response is not an immutable pin.
- Supported claims: `qudt:Unit` defines the scale used to measure quantities; schema includes quantity, unit, dimensional, and conversion concepts. The inspected `qudt:QuantityValue` description is minimal and does not establish a complete mapping.
- Reuse/license status: embedded rights metadata states CC BY 4.0, with attribution to QUDT.org. Separate embedded metadata identifies UCUM-derived material and its license conditions.
- Unresolved gates: select immutable schema and unit/quantity vocabulary releases; inspect selected unit definitions, dependency licenses, and UCUM conditions; specify gauge/absolute and reference-condition semantics. No blanket unit equivalence or conversion correctness claim is made.

### REF-STD-003: PROV-O

- Source/version: [W3C Recommendation, 2013-04-30](https://www.w3.org/TR/2013/REC-prov-o-20130430/), especially sections 3.1 and 4.
- Supported claims: PROV-O defines entities, activities, agents, and derivation/usage relationships. It supports bounded provenance mappings, not LIONG publication or approval policy.
- Reuse/license status: specification carries W3C copyright and document-use rules. It is publicly readable; no copy of the ontology is included in this task.
- Unresolved gates: pin the OWL artifact, inspect its exact license and imports, and check the selected terms' restrictions. Historical reconstruction remains a local design obligation.

### REF-STD-004: SOSA/SSN

- Source/version: [W3C/OGC Recommendation, 2017-10-19](https://www.w3.org/TR/2017/REC-vocab-ssn-20171019/), especially observation, feature-of-interest, phenomenon-time, and result-time definitions.
- Additional artifact: live [SOSA namespace RDF](https://www.w3.org/ns/sosa/), inspected for license declarations, not pinned as the 2017 serialization.
- Supported claims: an observation is an act of estimating or calculating a property's value. Its result, feature of interest, and times are distinct. These support a candidate measurement model through the equipment bridge.
- Reuse/license status: recommendation has W3C/OGC document notices. Live RDF lists `http://www.w3.org/Consortium/Legal/2015/copyright-software-and-document` and `http://www.opengeospatial.org/ogc/Software`.
- Access note: the fetch tool rejected the large recommendation response; direct public HTTP retrieval supplied the relevant definitions.
- Unresolved gates: freeze the desired recommendation and matching RDF artifacts; inspect dependency closure and notices; choose a bounded subset rather than importing all SSN axioms.

### REF-STD-005: Web Annotation Data Model

- Source/version: [W3C Recommendation, 2017-02-23](https://www.w3.org/TR/2017/REC-annotation-model-20170223/).
- Supported claims: annotations relate bodies and targets. Selectors can address resource segments, but supported selector/media combinations vary. This supports an evidence-locator pattern, not inferred engineering connectivity.
- Reuse/license status: W3C document-use notice. The [2015 W3C document license](https://www.w3.org/Consortium/Legal/2015/doc-license) was also inspected. It distinguishes document copying, limited implementation-oriented derivatives, and code components.
- Unresolved gates: inspect the exact vocabulary and JSON-LD context licenses if redistributed. Define immutable artifact IDs, page addressing, coordinate frames, rasterization, rotation, and crop transforms locally.

### REF-STD-006: IOF Core and Maintenance

- Source/version: [IOF release browser 202603](https://spec.industrialontologies.org/portal/release/202603/) and [maintenance work order record](https://spec.industrialontologies.org/portal/release/202603/maintenance/MaintenanceWorkOrderRecord.html).
- Supported claims: the portal uses BFO-based industrial concepts. The inspected term IRI is `https://spec.industrialontologies.org/ontology/construct/MaintenanceWorkOrderRecord`, defined in `https://spec.industrialontologies.org/ontology/maintenance/Maintenance/`.
- Definition evidence: the term describes a maintenance process and is input to such a process. The page calls its definition provisional because purely supporting maintenance activities do not satisfy it.
- Reuse/license status: portal and inspected term page state MIT. Exact RDF/OWL artifacts and imported BFO/Core dependency licenses were not inspected.
- Unresolved gates: evaluate foundation compatibility, term maturity, imports, and work-order mismatch before any subclass or equivalence assertion. Proposal is limited reference/mapping assessment, not foundational adoption.

### REF-STD-007: IDO/POSC Caesar

- Source attempted: [POSC Caesar reference data service](https://rds.posccaesar.org/) and [`ontology/lis14/ont/core`](https://rds.posccaesar.org/ontology/lis14/ont/core).
- Version inspected: none. Both public requests returned HTTP 403.
- Supported claims: this entry records a candidate and the access failure only. The PPC shortlist identifies IDO/POSC Caesar as an industrial asset/property reference, but this inspection did not independently verify term definitions.
- Reuse/license status: unverified. Public reference data access would not establish reuse rights for ISO publications or every related ontology.
- Unresolved gates: obtain a primary accessible artifact, release/version IRI, license, definitions, and imports. Do not implement an IDO mapping from this entry.

### REF-STD-008: pyDEXPI compatibility

- Source/version: [`README.md`](https://github.com/process-intelligence-research/pyDEXPI/blob/83e5a11c4af3635ad12290a4dbe310480eb6d7a3/README.md) and [`LICENSE`](https://github.com/process-intelligence-research/pyDEXPI/blob/83e5a11c4af3635ad12290a4dbe310480eb6d7a3/LICENSE), inspected on `master` at `83e5a11c4af3635ad12290a4dbe310480eb6d7a3`.
- Supported claims: README explicitly supports DEXPI 1.3 and describes loading Proteus XML through `ProteusSerializer`. Its conversion and graph utilities are candidate legacy tooling, not proof of DEXPI 2.0 support.
- Reuse/license status: AGPL version 3 or later, as stated in the license's program notice. No software copied or executed.
- Unresolved gates: assess copyleft obligations for intended use and any bundled data separately; verify exact input/output formats and fidelity. No native 2.0 reader/writer claim is supported.
- Access note: an initial `main` URL returned 404; repository metadata identified `master`.
- 2.0 support, accessed 2026-10-13: the latest release, v1.2.0 (2026-04-14), still supports DEXPI 1.3. In [issue 6](https://github.com/process-intelligence-research/pyDEXPI/issues/6), on 2.0 support, the maintainer wrote on 2026-07-28 that it would come in the upcoming months, with no date.

### REF-STD-009: DEXPI GraphicBuilder

- Source/version: [GitHub README](https://github.com/DEXPI/GraphicBuilder/blob/dbbca4555f9438bbef851d62851dd7e7f07a0911/README.md), `master` at `dbbca4555f9438bbef851d62851dd7e7f07a0911`.
- Supported claims: deprecated GitHub repository points to [GitLab GraphicBuilder](https://gitlab.com/dexpi/GraphicBuilder).
- Reuse/license status: current GitLab code and license unverified.
- Unresolved gates: inspect current release, accepted encoding, renderer fidelity, and license before use. No native DEXPI 2.0 compatibility claim is made.

### REF-STD-010: bpmn2dexpi

- Source/version: [GitHub repository](https://github.com/skhella/bpmn2dexpi), README on `main` at `f198a5b0b5ee90a829895b728beebd8c05903c03`, inspected 2026-10-13.
- Supported claims: README states that `--validate` checks existing DEXPI 2.0 Process and Plant files against the XSD and five information-model checks: property names and kinds, data types, reference targets, cardinality, and class existence. It ships DEXPI 2.0 copies of `Core.xml`, `Plant.xml` and `Process.xml`. It targets 2.0, not 2.0.1. It runs on Node.js.
- Reuse/license status: README states MIT. No software copied or executed.
- Unresolved gates: 2.0.1 support. Kept out of the slice ([DEC-069](decisions/DEC-069-bpmn2dexpi-recorded-not-used.md)).

## Data references

### REF-DATA-001: DEXPI 2.0 reference P&ID

- Source/version: [official 2.0 appendix](https://dexpi.org/specification/2.0/html/appendix/reference_pid.html), [XML](https://dexpi.org/specification/2.0/html/_static/reference_pid.xml), and linked [SVG](https://dexpi.org/specification/2.0/html/_images/reference_pid.svg).
- Artifact inspected: XML SHA-256 `f068ad94a18dd089afa3fc224d92056b08ee0059bd06686c68190c0b789ae2b1`. Its root is `Model`, with name `example` and URI `http://www.example.org`.
- Supported claims: XML uses Core and Plant imports under `/models/2.0.0/` and contains a `Core/EngineeringModel`. The appendix presents it as an illustration of the Plant model. The SVG link was inspected, not its visual content.
- Reuse/license status: governing specification page states CC BY 4.0. No independent per-download license notice was established for XML/SVG. Confirm coverage and attribution before redistribution.
- Access failure: `https://data.dexpi.org/models/2.0.0/Core.xml` and `https://data.dexpi.org/models/2.0.0/Plant.xml` failed TLS certificate hostname verification. Verification was not disabled. On 2026-10-13 `data.dexpi.org` did not respond. [DEC-062](decisions/DEC-062-vendored-model-files.md) has LIONG keep pinned copies of the model files instead. On 2026-10-14 `data.dexpi.org` served a certificate for `my.exacon.cloud`. The 2.0.1 copies are pinned in `standards/dexpi/2.0.1` ([DEC-074](decisions/DEC-074-dexpi-2-0-1-pinned-files.md)).
- Unresolved gates: acquire authentic imported artifacts through a trusted source; check complete dependency closure, SVG content, notices, and engineering completeness. XML well-formedness was checked, not XSD or semantic conformance.

### REF-DATA-002: DEXPI TrainingTestCases

- Source/version: [GitLab repository](https://gitlab.com/dexpi/TrainingTestCases), inspected `master` at `a23d61e2e089eb2ca464cd552f9ae580a2785963`.
- License evidence: [`LICENSE` at the pin](https://gitlab.com/dexpi/TrainingTestCases/-/blob/a23d61e2e089eb2ca464cd552f9ae580a2785963/LICENSE), retrieved through the public GitLab repository-files API, contains CC BY 4.0.
- Inspected paths: root tree, `dexpi 1.3/example pids`, and `dexpi 1.3/example pids/C01 DEXPI Reference P&ID`. C01 contains `C01V04-VER.EX01.xml`, `.svg`, `.html`, and `C01V04.pptx`. The XML was fetched at the pin and parsed; its root is `PlantModel`.
- Supported claims: repository separates DEXPI 1.2 and 1.3; example directories include equipment/nozzles, control, off-page connection, and intersection cases. File content and correctness were not audited across the collection.
- Reuse/license status: concrete CC BY 4.0 repository license supports reuse assessment beyond mere public access. Retain source attribution, license link, and change notices; inspect selected artifacts for exclusions or third-party rights.
- Migration evidence: [old GitHub TestCases README](https://github.com/DEXPI/TestCases/blob/09e9eddcb9da510ca6c103a01816b2629e903745/README.md) redirects to GitLab. Initial guessed GitHub `DEXPI/TrainingTestCases` returned 404; this is not evidence that the dataset is unavailable.
- Unresolved gates: choose and hash files, assess drawing quality and ground truth, confirm notices, and define explicit legacy-to-2.0 conversion tests. Do not report legacy input coverage as native 2.0 coverage.

### REF-DATA-003: proposed LIONG synthetic corpus

- Source/version: future project-authored artifacts under [LIONG-006](LIONG-006-synthetic-data.md); no release or files exist from this task.
- Supported claims: approved requirements permit clearly labeled synthetic data and require known structured cases. This entry proposes a provenance category, not a completed dataset.
- Reuse/license status: pending original creation and repository licensing decision. Reused symbols, templates, or public drawings retain applicable source obligations.
- Unresolved gates: specify generation rules, authorship, expected graphs, seeded revisions, attribution, review evidence, and public-versus-synthetic evaluation separation.

## Technology references

These entries consolidate the technology inspection in
[LIONG-007](LIONG-007-stack-and-architecture.md#version-and-source-evidence).
Access date: 2026-10-05 UTC. Candidate versions are not dependency locks.
Provider documentation is rolling and must be rechecked before use.

| ID | Primary source and inspected state | Supported claim and remaining gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| REF-TECH-001 | [PPC technology baseline at the pinned commit](https://github.com/aadehamid/pearland-petroleum-corporation/blob/01027a84be5d453cbb4e2ea091e4884729918b15/docs/PPC-002_Enterprise_Architecture_and_Technology_Stack.md) | Documented responsibilities, not runnable components; same repository evidence as REF-PPC-001 |
| REF-TECH-002 | PostgreSQL [version policy](https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/) and [license](https://www.postgresql.org/about/licence/); 18.6 observed | PostgreSQL License and supported release information; server/driver/image and recovery compatibility remain unlocked |
| REF-TECH-003 | Neo4j [edition documentation](https://neo4j.com/docs/operations-manual/current/introduction/), [licensing](https://neo4j.com/licensing/), [2026.09.0 license](https://github.com/neo4j/neo4j/blob/2026.09.0/LICENSE.txt) | Community GPLv3; edition-specific constraints, driver/runtime, backup, packaging obligations, and snapshot behavior require verification |

# DEC-086: W-SP's records map to DEXPI 2.0.1 through DEC-077's mapping, with sps identifier contexts, hand valves as OperatedValve and LT as category L

Status: Decided
Date: 2026-10-19

## Context

MILESTONE-001b takes W-SP through the same slice as MILESTONE-001
([DEC-042](DEC-042-w-sp-scn-001-first.md)), so the records `scripts/extract_sps.py`
writes ([DEC-085](DEC-085-sps-extraction-records.md)) must become DEXPI 2.0.1 files that
pass [DEC-064](DEC-064-four-stage-dexpi-validation.md)'s four stages, round-trip to
identical bytes, and parse back to W-SP's answer-key graph.
[DEC-077](DEC-077-dexpi-mapping.md) mapped only the Plant 3D-style records. W-SP adds
what R0 lacks: hand valves (HV), a level transmitter (LT), one line number drawn as two
runs on two drawings, GUID keys instead of whole-number object IDs, and attribute
predicates named as the SmartPlant-style rows name them (`tag_lead`, `link_sense`). The
agent decided the extension during the MILESTONE-001b night run, under the owner's
delegation in [DEC-080](DEC-080-milestone-001b-night-delegation.md). The owner can
reverse any of it.

## Decision

1. **One mapping, two backends.** `scripts/dexpi_generate.py` keeps DEC-077's mapping
   and holds what differs between the backends' records in a table, `BACKENDS`, chosen
   by the records' `source_id`. A source with no entry is refused. R0's output is
   byte-for-byte what it was before.
2. **Identity.** An item carries its GUID in a `PersistentIdentifier` with context
   `sps/DesignItem.ItemGuid`, a pipe segment with `sps/LineDepiction.DepictionGuid`,
   and a drawing's `PlantMetaData` with `sps/Sheet.SheetGuid`, following DEC-077's
   `table.column` form. The parser rebuilds `sps:item:<GUID>`, `sps:line:<GUID>` and
   `sps:sheet:<GUID>` from the context and value. File-local ids are the sps table
   and the GUID, with hyphens made underscores, such as `Vessel_4E781C49_...` and
   `LineDepiction_A80BEDD0_...`, as DEC-077 item 4 builds `Equipment_101`.
3. **Hand valves.** An HV valve is `Plant/Piping.OperatedValve` with its tag in
   `PipingComponentNumber` and no `ActuatingSystem`. The pinned Plant model has no
   class for a manually operated valve. It defines OperatedValve as a valve with "an
   external means of operation", naming a handwheel or lever as examples, and
   its subclasses, such as `BallValve` and `GateValve`, each name a valve body type.
   W-SP stores no body type. The sps fitting rows store no tag parts, so a valve's
   letters are the part of its tag before the first hyphen; letters outside the table
   are refused, as DEC-077 refuses an unknown XV-style tag type.
4. **Level transmitter.** LT is a `ProcessInstrumentationFunction` with category "L"
   and functions "T", added to PI's fixed table. Its number is the row's tag number,
   and its parent is a sensing location on an `InstrumentNozzle` of the vessel, as for
   PI in DEC-077.
5. **Line 301 across two drawings.** DEC-077 groups the segments on a drawing into one
   `PipingNetworkSystem` per line prefix and number. Run A's three segments therefore
   sit in `PipingNetworkSystem_L_301` in DEMO-PID-101's file, and run B's two in the
   system of the same id in DEMO-PID-102's file, each with `LineNumber` 301. DEXPI 2.0.1

# Brick: A Uniform Metadata Schema for Buildings #

## What is Brick? #

Brick is an open-source effort to standardize semantic descriptions of the physical, logical and virtual assets in buildings and the relationships between them. Brick consists of an extensible dictionary of terms and concepts in and around buildings, a set of relationships for linking and composing concepts together, and a flexible data model permitting seamless integration of Brick with existing tools and databases. Through the use of powerful Semantic Web technology, Brick can describe the broad set of idiosyncratic and custom features, assets and subsystems found across the building stock in a consistent matter.

## Getting Started #

- Check out Brick development on GitHub to file bugs, contribute, or learn more about the project
- Download the latest Brick stable or nightly release from the Brick releases page
- Read the Brick developer documentation to learn how to use Brick in your own projects
- Browse the new ontology documentation to explore the Brick ontology and its concepts
- Join the Google Group to discuss Brick with the community: Brick Schema Google Group

## Benefits of Brick #

Adopting Brick as the canonical description of a building enables the following:

- Brick lowers the cost of deploying analytics, energy efficiency measures and intelligent controls across buildings
- Brick presents an integrated, cross-vendor representation of the multitude of subsystems in modern buildings: HVAC, lighting, fire, security and others
- Brick simplifies the development of smart analytics and control applications
- Brick reduces the reliance upon the non-standard, unstructured labels endemic to building management systems

# Brick v1.5.0

## New Features

- Controller and Point Group model: adds `brick:Controller`, `brick:controls`/`brick:isControlledBy`, and `brick:hosts`/`brick:isHostedBy` relationships for modeling BAS controllers and the points they expose (#724, #753)
- Automation and Point Collections: adds `brick:Automation_Collection` and `brick:Point_Collection` for organizing automation bundles and point groups. `brick:Point_Collection` is not a subclass of `brick:Automation_Collection` (#747, #754, #792)
- Plants: adds `brick:Plant` (a subclass of `brick:Equipment`) with `brick:Boiler_Plant` and `brick:Chiller_Plant`, plus SHACL shapes for how plants are composed with `rec:includes` (#794)
- Plumbing points and classes: first batch of plumbing classes from #684, including `brick:Domestic_Hot_Water_Plant`, `brick:Domestic_Cold_Water_System`, `brick:Water_Leak_Sensor`, `brick:High_Pressure_Alarm`/`brick:Low_Pressure_Alarm`, `brick:On_Off_Cycle_Count_Sensor`, and the `Brine` and `Condensate` substances (#795)
- Return path modeling: adds support for modeling return air/water paths in HVAC systems (#774)
- Lighting changes for REC working group: initial alignment of Brick lighting classes with the REC lighting working group (#756)
- Add `Unit_Heater` class (#779)
- Add valve as parent for metering valves (#750)
- Add additional substances (#760)
- Add all numeric data types for entity properties (#732)
- Aliases for switch subclasses (#746)
- Add definitions for relationships (#788) and for 71 equipment and system classes (#802)
- IAQ sensor deployment example (#791)

## Deprecation Changes

- `brick:Collection` is being phased out in favor of `rec:Collection`: `brick:Collection` is now a subclass of `rec:Collection`, all built-in collection classes (e.g. `brick:System`, `brick:Loop`, `brick:Automation_Collection`, `brick:Point_Collection`) inherit from it and use `rec:includes` for membership. New models should use `rec:Collection` directly. `brick:Collection` is not marked `owl:deprecated`, so existing data using Brick collection classes does not raise deprecation warnings (#775, #803, #814)
- `brick:connectedTo` removed (#751)
- Deprecated class definitions moved out of main definitions and into `bricksrc/deprecations.py` (#727, #800)
- Fix misspelled deprecation for `brick:Occupied_Zone_Air_Temperature_Setpoint` (#815, #810)

## Fixes and Improvements

- REC spaces accepted wherever Brick locations are: System/Loop/Portfolio `rec:includes`, entity properties, `brick:hasAddress`, meter rules, and Point/Equipment exclusivity now handle REC spaces, and inverse/symmetric inference runs on REC entities (#811)
- `rec:Architecture` added to location relationship domains/ranges: `brick:hasLocation`, `brick:isLocationOf`, and related relationships now accept `rec:Architecture` entities, fixing SHACL validation errors when using REC location classes (#757)
- Allow QUDT quantity kinds for `brick:hasQuantity` on Points (#809)
- Fix meter inference rules: meters are no longer typed as points (#805, #808)
- Remove duplicate shapes for `brick:isPointOf` (#789)
- Fix prefixes in generated TTL files (`bacnet1:`, `ns1:`) (#810)
- `brick:Collection` stays a subclass of `brick:Entity` after being made a subclass of `rec:Collection` (#820)
- Generated files define only the Brick ontology: leftover ontology headers from REC and the REC patches are no longer included (#817)
- Chilled water system points restored: fixes missing points on chilled water system classes (#752)
- Clarify substance temperature definitions (#785)
- Update REC patches (#711)
- Fix extra properties in extensions going to wrong graph (#745)
- Fix issue #700: duplicate literal handling (#710, #708)
- Fix issue #719 (#720)

## Dependency Updates

- QUDT updated to 3.3.0 (#738, #772, #773, #786)
- REC patched to Brick 1.4 compatibility (#740)
- REC submodule updated: Brick's patched `rec:Riser`/`rec:PlumbingRiser` are removed, `brick:Riser` is now replaced by `rec:ServiceShaft`, and the `rec:Wing` patch now mirrors upstream REC (a subclass of `rec:SubBuilding`) (#821)
- Updated 223P usage and examples (#718)
- BACnet namespace unified to `http://data.ashrae.org/bacnet/`, and the `ref:` schema updated to use terms from the BACnet ontology (#806, #766, #816)

## Contributors

Thank you to everyone who contributed to Brick v1.5.0! In descending order of merged PRs:

- @ektrah
- @metesaka
- @jbkoh
- @sappling
- @connorjcantrell
- @fennibay
- @JoelBender
- @mhusm
- @steveraysteveray

# Brick v1.5.0

## New Features

- Controller and Point Group model: adds `brick:Controller`, `brick:controls`/`brick:isControlledBy`, and `brick:hosts`/`brick:isHostedBy` relationships for modeling BAS controllers and the points they expose (#724, #753)
- Automation and Point Collections: adds `brick:Automation_Collection` and `brick:Point_Collection` for organizing automation bundles and point groups. `brick:Point_Collection` is not a subclass of `brick:Automation_Collection` (#747, #754, #792)
- Plants: adds `brick:Plant` (a subclass of `brick:Equipment`) with `brick:Boiler_Plant` and `brick:Chiller_Plant`, plus SHACL shapes for how plants are composed with `rec:includes` (#794)
- Plumbing points and classes: first batch of plumbing classes from #684, including `brick:Domestic_Hot_Water_Plant`, `brick:Domestic_Cold_Water_System`, `brick:Water_Leak_Sensor`, `brick:High_Pressure_Alarm`/`brick:Low_Pressure_Alarm`, `brick:On_Off_Cycle_Count_Sensor`, and the `Brine` and `Condensate` substances (#795)
- Return path modeling: adds support for modeling return air/water paths in HVAC systems (#774)
- Lighting changes for REC working group: initial alignment of Brick lighting classes with the REC lighting working group (#756)
- Add `Unit_Heater` class (#779)
- Add valve as parent for metering valves (#750)
- Add additional substances (#760)
- Add all numeric data types for entity properties (#732)
- Aliases for switch subclasses (#746)
- Add definitions for relationships (#788) and for 71 equipment and system classes (#802)
- IAQ sensor deployment example (#791)

## Deprecation Changes

- `brick:Collection` is being phased out in favor of `rec:Collection`: `brick:Collection` is now a subclass of `rec:Collection`, all built-in collection classes (e.g. `brick:System`, `brick:Loop`, `brick:Automation_Collection`, `brick:Point_Collection`) inherit from it and use `rec:includes` for membership. New models should use `rec:Collection` directly. `brick:Collection` is not marked `owl:deprecated`, so existing data using Brick collection classes does not raise deprecation warnings (#775, #803, #814)
- `brick:connectedTo` removed (#751)
- Deprecated class definitions moved out of main definitions and into `bricksrc/deprecations.py` (#727, #800)
- Fix misspelled deprecation for `brick:Occupied_Zone_Air_Temperature_Setpoint` (#815, #810)

## Fixes and Improvements

- REC spaces accepted wherever Brick locations are: System/Loop/Portfolio `rec:includes`, entity properties, `brick:hasAddress`, meter rules, and Point/Equipment exclusivity now handle REC spaces, and inverse/symmetric inference runs on REC entities (#811)
- `rec:Architecture` added to location relationship domains/ranges: `brick:hasLocation`, `brick:isLocationOf`, and related relationships now accept `rec:Architecture` entities, fixing SHACL validation errors when using REC location classes (#757)
- Allow QUDT quantity kinds for `brick:hasQuantity` on Points (#809)
- Fix meter inference rules: meters are no longer typed as points (#805, #808)
- Remove duplicate shapes for `brick:isPointOf` (#789)
- Fix prefixes in generated TTL files (`bacnet1:`, `ns1:`) (#810)
- `brick:Collection` stays a subclass of `brick:Entity` after being made a subclass of `rec:Collection` (#820)
- Generated files define only the Brick ontology: leftover ontology headers from REC and the REC patches are no longer included (#817)
- Chilled water system points restored: fixes missing points on chilled water system classes (#752)
- Clarify substance temperature definitions (#785)
- Update REC patches (#711)
- Fix extra properties in extensions going to wrong graph (#745)
- Fix issue #700: duplicate literal handling (#710, #708)
- Fix issue #719 (#720)

## Dependency Updates

- QUDT updated to 3.3.0 (#738, #772, #773, #786)
- REC patched to Brick 1.4 compatibility (#740)
- REC submodule updated: Brick's patched `rec:Riser`/`rec:PlumbingRiser` are removed, `brick:Riser` is now replaced by `rec:ServiceShaft`, and the `rec:Wing` patch now mirrors upstream REC (a subclass of `rec:SubBuilding`) (#821)
- Updated 223P usage and examples (#718)
- BACnet namespace unified to `http://data.ashrae.org/bacnet/`, and the `ref:` schema updated to use terms from the BACnet ontology (#806, #766, #816)

## Contributors

Thank you to everyone who contributed to Brick v1.5.0! In descending order of merged PRs:

- @gtfierro
- @ektrah
- @metesaka
- @jbkoh
- @sappling
- @connorjcantrell
- @fennibay
- @JoelBender
- @mhusm
- @steveraysteveray

### REF-STD-011: Brick

- Source/version: [brickschema.org](https://brickschema.org/), [GitHub releases](https://github.com/BrickSchema/Brick/releases), and [repository](https://github.com/BrickSchema/Brick), inspected 2026-11-08 UTC.

- Inspected paths: the site's introduction page; the v1.5.0 release notes; the tagged tree's README (`README.md` calls Brick an open-source, BSD-licensed development effort), `LICENSE` (BSD-3-Clause, copyright "Brick Consortium, Inc. 2016-2026"), tree listing, and `bricksrc/`; the ontology's releases history from v1.4.0 to v1.5.0. The repository generates the ontology serializations with `generate_brick.py`; the tree inspected carries no generated `Brick.ttl`.
- Model observed from the release notes and history: Brick describes building assets as `brick:Equipment`, `brick:Location`, and `brick:Point` entities, linked by relationships such as `hasPoint`/`isPointOf`, `hasLocation`/`isLocationOf`, `hasPart`/`isPartOf`, and `isFedBy`. Since v1.4.0 relationships use SHACL property shapes instead of RDFS domain/range. Point entity properties resolve quantities through QUDT quantity kinds: v1.4.4 deprecated home-grown Brick quantity classes in favor of `qudt:` quantity kinds, and v1.4.2 to v1.5.0 update them (v1.5.0 moved to QUDT 3.3.0). v1.4.0 began phasing Brick location classes out in favor of RealEstateCore (REC); v1.5.0 makes Brick collection classes subclasses of `rec:Collection` and adds controllers with `controls`/`isControlledBy` and `hosts`/`isHostedBy` relationships, plus SHACL shapes for plant composition via `rec:includes`; it removes `brick:connectedTo` and aligns lighting classes with the REC working group.
- Supported claims: a deployed, actively maintained metadata schema (releases in October 2026) for building physical, logical, and virtual assets with a relationship model and SHACL constraints. Its model corroborates two register positions: quantities belong to a shared vocabulary (QUDT, [REF-STD-002](#ref-std-002-qudt)) rather than to home-grown classes, and relationship validation belongs to shapes rather than domain/range axioms. It is a reference precedent for the measurement and equipment bridge described under SOSA/SSN ([REF-STD-004](#ref-std-004-sosassn)): a point attaches to equipment, carries a quantity kind, and sits at a location, with sensors, setpoints, alarms and commands as point subclasses, and `isFedBy` for how equipment feeds one another.
- Reuse/license status: the repository is BSD-3-Clause (Brick Consortium, Inc.); the README describes the whole effort as BSD-licensed. No ontology serialization was copied or vendored in this task.
- Unresolved gates: Brick's domain is building automation (HVAC, lighting, fire, security), not process plants; it has no classes for LIONG's process equipment, nozzles, pipe runs, or P&ID instrument loops, so its classes cannot be the published graph's core vocabulary. Any use is a bounded mapping bridge for instrument-point semantics, pending an owner decision record. Gates before any reuse: pin and hash the generated v1.5.0 serialization; confirm the serialization's own license and attribution strings (the deprecation tables name REC at `w3id.org/rec` and BACnet at `data.ashrae.org/bacnet/`, so any vendored file imports those dependencies and their licenses); choose the bounded subset; test a mapping against W-SP's LT and PI records ([DEC-086](decisions/DEC-086-sps-dexpi-mapping.md)) before asserting one. Recorded as a candidate for the owner's review, not an adoption.

Restorable parts check out. I verified against the live Brick sources that the version, tag, release date, release notes (SHACL switch in v1.4.0, quantity-class deprecations in v1.4.4, QUDT updates from v1.4.2 to 3.3.0 in v1.5.0, REC phase-out, `rec:Collection` subclassing, controllers, `rec:includes` shapes, `brick:connectedTo` removal, REC lighting alignment), the 2026-11-07 nightly at `3fdb570`, the BSD-3-Clause LICENSE (copyright "Brick Consortium, Inc. 2016-2026"), the README wording, and the intro page's "physical, logical and virtual assets" and subsystem list all match REF-STD-011. The round-1 hook hold is closed: `scripts/hooks/pre-push` at the head is identical to `main`'s blob, and the zip still matches the worktree (`scripts/hooks/pre-push` is not an archived file, so no rebuild was needed).

One blocking finding remains, unchanged by this commit:

1. **Unsourced corroboration claim / misattributed register positions** — `docs/LIONG-REF-001-reference-register.md` line 121: "Its model corroborates two register positions: quantities belong to a shared vocabulary (QUDT, REF-STD-002) rather than to home-grown classes, and relationship validation belongs to shapes rather than domain/range axioms." Neither position is a register position.
   - REF-STD-002's supported claims are only that `qudt:Unit` defines the scale used to measure quantities, that the schema includes quantity/unit/dimensional/conversion concepts, and that the inspected `qudt:QuantityValue` description is minimal and does not establish a complete mapping. It never states that quantities belong to QUDT rather than to home-grown classes, and no other register row does. Note also the versions: this entry says v1.5.0 moved to QUDT 3.3.0, while REF-STD-002's inspected schema is 3.5.2 — two separate inspections that the sentence joins.
   - No register row states that relationship validation belongs to shapes rather than domain/range axioms. `docs/LIONG-007-stack-and-architecture.md` (line 67) lists SHACL as "Adapt separation of meaning; defer services" and to "test selected SHACL tooling only if required" — a deferral, not that position.
   - Concrete reason: under the register's own evidence rule (an inspected source supports only the claims listed in its entry) and REVIEW_STANDARDS' rule that records claim only what their sources show, Brick's release notes cannot corroborate positions the register does not hold. The v1.4.4 note does show Brick deprecating its quantity classes for QUDT quantity kinds, but that is a fact about Brick, not a register position to cite.
2. **Misattribution to a cited entry** — `docs/LIONG-REF-001-reference-register.md` line 121, the sentence after the colon: it presents the point/equipment/quantity-kind/location/`isFedBy` structure as "the measurement and equipment bridge described under SOSA/SSN (REF-STD-004)". REF-STD-004 (line 64) registers only the observation model — result, feature of interest, and times distinct, supporting a candidate measurement model through the equipment bridge — and does not describe that Brick structure. The description should be Brick's own (it fits the release notes and `bricksrc`), not attributed to REF-STD-004.

Rewriting the "Supported claims" bullet to state only what the inspected sources show (with the precedent claim expressed as LIONG's own reading, not as a corroborated register position) clears both points; no other change blocks the merge.
